Pull request creation is refused for this account (`CreatePullRequest` FORBIDDEN). The branch is on the fork.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f045-clipboard-pixel-budget?expand=1

Head: `985a5d708e74de790c7e3c2bae188aafac389238` on `SebTardif:fix/f045-clipboard-pixel-budget`

## What Problem

Pasting a clipboard image decodes the whole bitmap before the 10 MB attachment cap.

## User Impact

A pasted image whose encoded bytes or decoded pixels would pass 10 MB is dropped before the bitmap is allocated. A paste that fits still becomes a PNG attachment.

## Why

A file attachment is rejected from its length before it is read. The clipboard path decoded the frame with GetSoftwareBitmapAsync, encoded PNG, and only then compared the PNG size with the cap. A compact image can expand to a much larger bitmap. The paste now rejects a stream that is already over the cap, and rejects the decoder's raw or oriented pixel size, before that decode. The PNG size check still runs after encoding.

## Evidence

`ExceedsDecodedPixelBudget` did not exist, so the new tests failed to compile (`CS0117`).

After the helper, those three tests passed: one pixel past the cap is rejected, a bitmap exactly at the cap is accepted, and `uint.MaxValue` by `uint.MaxValue` at 4 bytes per pixel is rejected.

`ClipboardPaste_ChecksThePixelBudgetBeforeDecoding` passed. The stream cap and `ExceedsDecodedPixelBudget` both appear before `GetSoftwareBitmapAsync`.

`./build.ps1` succeeded.

Shared tests passed 4663, skipped 24, total 4687.

Tray tests passed 4475, skipped 0, total 4475.

## Real Behavior Proof

- Environment tested: the shared attachment budget and the clipboard source order. The tray window was not opened.
- Commit tested: `985a5d708e74de790c7e3c2bae188aafac389238`
- Steps: `dotnet test` filters `ExceedsDecodedPixelBudget` and `ClipboardPaste_ChecksThePixelBudgetBeforeDecoding`.
- Evidence: the three budget tests passed in 108 ms. The call-order test passed in 154 ms.
- Observed result: dimensions that decode past 10 MB are rejected before `GetSoftwareBitmapAsync`.
- Screenshot: no.
- Not verified: a live paste was not performed. A rejected paste returns no attachment and writes no log line, and producing the oversized decoded bitmap is the allocation this change avoids.

## Required proof pools

- `none`: no installer, WSL gateway, MXC, or ARM64 pool applies.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities? No
- Secrets or tokens handling changed? No
- New or changed network calls? No
- Command or tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

title: Gateway capability tracking

body:
## Summary
Sandboxed Python 3.11 loopback IPC fails with WSAEACCES (10013) through Windows Node system.run. Please clarify whether same-invocation loopback is supported without disabling AppContainer or granting a blanket loopback exemption.

## Environment
- Companion 2026.9.8-1
- Installed PDB SourceLink commit: 2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114
- Windows version reported by device.info: Microsoft Windows 10.0.26300
- Python 3.11

## Observed diagnostics (October 21, 2026)
A bounded socket probe inside the node execution context, separately for 127.0.0.1 and ::1, could bind/listen. Nonblocking connect_ex returned 10035; select signaled the exceptional set, and SO_ERROR returned 10013. Token inspection reported TokenIsAppContainer=1, TokenHasRestrictions=1, TokenElevation=0.
Python socketpair implementation can then hang at listener.accept after catching the nonblocking connect condition without detecting the asynchronous denial. Ordinary operator PowerShell execution worked outside this node context; this does not prove the companion has been repaired.
The exact denying WFP rule has NOT been identified. We are not asserting a specific firewall defect or a security vulnerability.

## Source inspection
At the above installed SourceLink revision, src/OpenClaw.Shared/Mxc/MxcConfigBuilder.cs Build() adds internetClient when AllowOutbound is true and emits network defaultPolicy plus enforcementMode=capabilities. We did not find Build() mapping AllowLocalNetwork or AllowedHosts/BlockedHosts to the emitted configuration. Declared DTO fields alone do not establish backend support.
Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Mxc/MxcConfigBuilder.cs

## Requested clarification
1. Is loopback IPC between sockets created within one sandboxed invocation supported in this version? If not, please document that limitation.
2. Is there a supported narrowly scoped capability preserving containment without exposing unrelated host services? Please identify the version, mapping, verification and cleanup procedure.
3. If a newer release addresses this, please link the implementing change/tests; we have not upgraded or relaxed policy.

Related: #1367 (closed capability inquiry). This report concerns an observed Python loopback failure on a different installed revision, rather than the SketchUp integration in that issue.

No sandbox disabling, blanket loopback exemption, firewall/ACL changes, or elevation were performed to work around the denial. No production code or services were modified for this report.

## What Problem

After a chat reset, a lifecycle end that arrives before the user message echo is dropped. Opening the buffered start then leaves the turn active.

Related: #1462. This is the dropped end, not every way a chat can stay on "Assistant is thinking".

Pull request creation is refused for this account (`CreatePullRequest` FORBIDDEN). The branch is on the fork.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f044-keep-reset-lifecycle-end?expand=1

Head: `480b5e2bcc690c4aed70b943b2b3fcf296a1147e` on `SebTardif:fix/f044-keep-reset-lifecycle-end`

## User Impact

A lifecycle end or error that arrives while the reset gate is still waiting is kept with that run. When the buffered start opens, the turn ends instead of staying active.

## Why

Starts that arrive before the echo are buffered. Ends and errors were not. The echo then opened the start with no matching end, so the thinking state stayed on.

## Evidence

Before the change, `Reset_EndBeforeEcho_DoesNotLeaveTheTurnActive` failed: after the echo, the turn was still active. After the change the turn is inactive.

`./build.ps1` succeeded.

Shared tests passed 4660, skipped 24, total 4684.

Tray tests passed 4471, skipped 0, total 4471. That includes the reset-state tests.

## Real Behavior Proof

- Environment tested: `ChatConversationState`, which owns the timeline `TurnActive` flag the composer uses for the thinking state. The tray window was not opened.
- Commit tested: `480b5e2bcc690c4aed70b943b2b3fcf296a1147e`
- Steps: reset the thread, send `hello` so the turn is active, deliver a lifecycle start and end for `new-run` before the echo, then deliver the user echo `hello`.
- Evidence before the fix: `Assert.False` on `TurnActive` failed because the value was still true.
- Evidence after the fix: the same steps leave `TurnActive` false. The 16 reset and conversation tests around that path passed.
- Screenshot: no.
- Not verified: the tray window was not opened, so the composer label was not read on screen.

## Required proof pools

- `none`: no installer, WSL gateway, MXC, or ARM64 pool applies. The turn flag is the conversation-state trace above.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities? No
- Secrets or tokens handling changed? No
- New or changed network calls? No
- Command or tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

body:
## What Problem

Opening Usage replaces the selected 7-day totals with the 30-day snapshot.

Pull request creation is refused for this account (`CreatePullRequest` FORBIDDEN, REST create 404). The branch is on the fork.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f037-usage-period?expand=1

Head: `70a4c754316209006ec493c92bda01df3be167df` on `SebTardif:fix/f037-usage-period`

## User Impact

Usage opens on 7 Days and keeps that period. A 30-day cost that arrived earlier does not move the selector or replace the totals. Choosing 30 Days still requests 30 days.

## Why

The page refresh asked for the selected period and also for a fixed 30-day cost. The first cost payload was applied even when its day count did not match the selector, and the selector then moved to that period. The branch requests status plus the selected period only. A payload applies when its day count is unspecified or within one day of the selection. The handshake may still request 30 days for the rest of the app. That payload does not paint the Usage page while 7 Days is selected.

## Evidence

Before this change, `ShouldApply_RejectsFirstMismatchedResponse` failed: a 30-day payload was accepted for a 7-day selection.

`./build.ps1` succeeded in the worktree. The Usage page sources were saved at 20:11 and the win-x64 exe was written at 20:13 local time on 2026-10-21.

Shared tests passed 4638, skipped 24, total 4662.

Tray tests passed 4462, skipped 0, total 4462. That run includes `UsageCostApplicationPolicyTests`.

## Real Behavior Proof

- Environment tested: Windows, non-dev win-x64 tray from that head, isolated `OPENCLAW_TRAY_DATA_DIR`, fixture gateway on port 61053.
- Commit tested: `70a4c754316209006ec493c92bda01df3be167df`
- Steps: start the tray against the fixture, wait for the handshake cost, then open `openclaw://hub/usage` and read the period selector with UI Automation.
- Evidence: at 20:14:12 the activity log recorded `[usage] 30d usage $0.00`. At 20:15:19 the usage deep link was handled and the log recorded `[usage] 7d usage $0.00`. body:
## Summary

After WSL gateway setup completes any AI-connect step (confirmed with Local AI; AI-connect is mandatory for WSL in the current wizard, so every WSL setup run hits this) and the tray app does its post-setup restart, **no chat window, hub window, or any other window appears at all** for several minutes (observed ~93s+ and counting in both reproductions below). The only window that eventually appears is Settings (Connection page), which does show the backend as healthy.

Found via two independent, fresh-pull reproductions (`b65006a6` and `c25f7ba0`), both clean builds on a fresh isolated profile.

## Current behavior

1. Fresh clean build, fresh isolated profile, fresh WSL distro.
2. Walk onboarding: Install a local Gateway (WSL) -> Balanced capabilities -> Install (succeeds) -> Connect your AI (mandatory, no skip reachable in a normal run) -> Local AI on this PC -> install completes, model verified, gateway reconfigured and running.
3. Click "Talk to my agent" on the finish page.
4. The tray app restarts. The restarted process is launched with `--post-setup-launch ai-v3:<hash>` (a native dashboard-handoff token), not the plain `"chat"` route string.
5. `openclaw-tray.log` shows `[WARN] Native setup destination failed (InvalidOperationException); phase: none; result: Unavailable.` at roughly the same point in both reproductions.
6. No window (chat, hub, or even an error dialog) appears. `EnumWindows` against the restarted process shows nothing for 2+ minutes.
7. Eventually, a Settings window (Connection page) appears on its own and correctly shows Connected/healthy operator and node state — but chat is never reached.

## Expected behavior

The post-restart window (chat, or at minimum a visible error/retry dialog) should appear promptly, or the failure should be surfaced to the user instead of leaving no window at all.

## Investigation notes (not fully confirmed, worth a maintainer's look)

- The restart routes through `ActivationRouter` -> `OpenNativeSetupCompletion` -> `SetupNativeHandoffLauncher.OpenAsync` for this `ai-v3:` token, which is architecturally separate from the plain `ShowHub`/`ShowWorkspace` restart path.
- `Logger.Warn` for this failure only logs the exception type, not its message, so the exact `InvalidOperationException` text wasn't recoverable from the log alone.
- Best-evidence hypothesis from reading the code (not confirmed with a debugger/instrumentation): `SetupGatewaySession.ConnectAsync` has a provenance/device-token check (`needsProvenance` true for a WSL-managed loopback gateway) that calls `provenanceService.InspectAsync` and can throw `InvalidOperationException` if the result doesn't match `ExpectedManagedGateway`. This check does not exist in the native-package gateway branch of `SetupNativeCompletionVerifier.VerifyAsync`, which would explain why a plain native-gateway setup doesn't hit this.
- Separately, whatever the actual failure is, `ShowNativeSetupFailureAsync` (or the broader `SetupNativeHandoffLauncher.OpenAsync` failure path) should produce a visible window/error dialog instead of leaving the user with nothing on screen — that's a bug independent of the root cause above.

## Reproduction

Deterministic across two separate fresh-pull attempts on `main` (`b65006a6`, `c25f7ba0`). Needs a WSL-capable Windows test machine; AI-connect is unavoidable in the current wizard flow for WSL.

## Related

This was originally mistaken for #1780 ("chat window stuck on Loading messages"), which was closed as not reproducing on current `main` after this different, no-window symptom kept reproducing instead in its place.

body:
### Bug type

Client bug (Windows Hub native chat + SSH tunnel lifecycle)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Windows Hub **v2026.9.8-1** (latest stable) native chat against a **2026.10.5** gateway (1b58cb9) over the built-in SSH tunnel is unusable, with a cascade failure:

1. Composer keyboard shortcuts are dead — **Enter and Ctrl+Enter do not submit**; only clicking the send button works.
2. Clicking send delivers the message (gateway-side `chat.send` triggers a full agent turn; model calls and the assistant reply are generated), but **no reply ever renders in the Hub** — the sent bubble stays gray indefinitely.
3. Within ~1–4 minutes the **entire app freezes** and must be force-closed.
4. After force-close, the Hub's tunnel `ssh.exe` survives as an **orphan holding local port 18789**; the next Hub start fails the tunnel with port-in-use. `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 18789` reports an OwningProcess PID that `tasklist` cannot resolve (ghost socket) until the OS reclaims it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.10.5 on Ubuntu (systemd user service, `bind: loopback`, `auth.mode: token`).
2. Hub setup: SSH-tunnel connection type (key-based SSH auth to the gateway host), gateway token auth, device pairing approved via `openclaw devices approve`.
3. Open a DM session in the Hub's native chat. Type a message. Try Enter / Ctrl+Enter (nothing happens). Click the send button.
4. Observe: message reaches the gateway and the assistant turn completes (visible in gateway journal), but no reply appears; the bubble stays gray; the app freezes within minutes; force-close leaves `ssh.exe` holding 18789.

### Expected behavior

- Enter/Ctrl+Enter submit the composed message.
- The assistant reply renders in the chat.
- No app freeze; tunnel process is terminated with the app.

### Actual behavior

See the four-point cascade above. Gateway-side journal evidence for step 2: the Hub's WebSocket connection polls `sessions.list` / `sessions.preview` successfully, `chat.send` starts the turn (model calls logged, reply generated), but **zero reply/event deliveries reach the Hub connection** in the same window.

Workaround that works: the **gateway-served browser Control UI over the same tunnel renders the session and full bidirectional chat fine** — suggesting the native client's event-stream consumption is what breaks, not the tunnel or the gateway.

### Additional context

- Client: OpenClaw Windows Tray `cli v2026.9.8-1` (from the standalone releases page, latest stable as of 2026-10-20).
- Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), Ubuntu, loopback bind.
- Note: the stable channel (v2026.9.8-1, latest) currently has no build whose native chat works against a 2026.10.5 gateway — as reported here the feature is unusable, not degraded.
- The SSH tunnel recovery path did not clean up the orphaned `ssh.exe` after the freeze.
- Happy to provide journal excerpts or run controlled reproductions on request.

Additional user report (2026-10-25): keyboard submission is unusable in **Windows Hub native Windows chat**, not browser Control UI.

The user explicitly reports that none of **Enter**, **Shift+Enter**, or **Ctrl+Enter** sends the composed chat message, and requested that this be reported upstream. Exact per-key effects (newline/no-op/caret movement) and mouse Send behavior have not yet been confirmed. This is a user observation, not a controlled reproduction by the reporting assistant.

Current Windows Hub version, Windows build, keyboard layout/IME state, and connection mode are unknown. Please do not infer the version or the SSH/freeze symptoms from the parent report; those additional symptoms are not asserted by this report.

Suggested reproduction/triage: open native chat, focus the composer, enter a short nonempty message, test Enter and Ctrl+Enter separately; also check Shift+Enter newline insertion and mouse Send independently. Verify with IME composition active and inactive if relevant.

Expected: the advertised send shortcut submits once; Shift+Enter preserves a normal newline, and a discoverable mouse Send action works. Shift+Enter not sending is not itself considered a defect.

Related: #1674 and closed #1766 document the OnKeyDown to OnPreviewKeyDown repair. This report does **not** establish a regression on a fix-containing version. Please clarify the currently supported stable build containing the repair and any version/reproduction details required to distinguish an older stable defect from a current regression.

## Root cause of "Enter / Ctrl+Enter do not submit" + verified fix

**Client**: `2026.9.8-1` (file version `2026.9.8.0`), Gateway `2026.10.6`, managed local gateway (no SSH tunnel), native chat (`UseLegacyWebChat=false`).

**Reported behaviour**: plain **Enter inserts a newline** (does not submit). `Ctrl+Alt+Enter` submits. The send button works.

**Code path**: `ReactorChatComposer.Render` creates the composer as a Reactor `TextBox` with `AcceptsReturn(true)`, then attaches its key handler via `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.ElementExtensions.OnKeyDown(...)`, i.e. a **bubbling** `KeyDown` handler.

`<Render>b__19` (IL, decompiled body):

```csharp
// slash menu handling first (Tab/Enter/Up/Down/Esc) ...
if (e.Key != VirtualKey.Enter) return;
if (InputKeyboardSource.GetKeyStateForCurrentThread(VirtualKey.Shift) & Down) return; // Shift+Enter => newline
e.Handled = true;
Send();                        // Send() no-ops when !vm.CanSend
```

**Root cause**: with `AcceptsReturn(true)` the `TextBox` class handler consumes Enter (inserts the newline) and marks the event handled before it bubbles, so the instance-level bubbling `KeyDown` handler never runs. `Ctrl+Alt+Enter` is not a text-editing chord, so the `TextBox` leaves it alone and the handler does receive it. Same mechanism explains Ctrl+Enter being dead.

**Fix (verified on 2026.9.8.0)**: attach the same handler to the tunnelling event instead of the bubbling one — `ElementExtensions.OnPreviewKeyDown` (same signature, `Action<object, KeyRoutedEventArgs>`) instead of `OnKeyDown`. No other change needed: the handler already ignores `Shift+Enter`, so `Shift+Enter` still inserts a newline and bare Enter now submits.

Alternatively `AddHandler(UIElement.KeyDownEvent, handler, handledEventsToo: true)` should work equally.

**How I verified**: applied the swap as a local IL patch to `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.dll` (2026.9.8.0), restarted, and pressed Enter in the composer — the message submits and the composer clears; `Shift+Enter` still produces a newline.

Side note (may be a separate issue): in the same build, `chat.send` has a hard-coded **5 s** response timeout (`OpenClaw.Shared.OpenClawGatewayClient.SendChatMessageForRunAsync`, `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)`). When the gateway takes longer to ack (e.g. `openclaw status` reports `reachable 6.17s` on this machine), the send is reported as "Timed out waiting for chat.send response from gateway" even though the message was delivered and the agent turn runs — and the draft is not cleared, so a retry can duplicate. Worth considering a longer timeout and/or clearing the draft on late ack.

Following up on this — the thread now has everything needed for a fix:

- @168062576-tech's root-cause analysis (Oct 28) pins the Enter-submission failure to the composer's bubbling `KeyDown` handler being pre-empted by the `TextBox` class handler (`AcceptsReturn(true)`), with a verified fix and the decompiled code path included.
- @willim-tuf's Oct 25 report confirms keyboard submission is still broken for users on the stable channel, on top of the original render-freeze / ghost-tunnel symptoms.

Current state for stable-channel users: native chat remains unusable against 2026.10.x gateways — the stable channel hasn't moved past `v2026.9.8-1`, while the alpha line has already reached `v2026.10.8-alpha.20`. Browser Control UI over the same tunnel works fine, so the gap is purely client-side.

Is there anything we can add to help this land — e.g. validating the proposed fix against a specific alpha build, or testing a patched build if one becomes available? Happy to verify on a real 2026.10.8 gateway setup.

body:
**What:** In the native chat composer, pressing Up arrow on an empty box should recall the previous sent message, and Down should step forward again (like a shell, and like the gateway's web chat).

**Why:** Re-sending or tweaking a recent message currently means retyping or copying it. The gateway's web chat (the "Use gateway's web chat interface" / `UseLegacyWebChat` path) already has this, so anyone who relies on it has to keep the legacy switch on. If that switch is ever removed, the native composer needs this too.

**Where:** `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ReactorChatComposer.cs`. `VirtualKey.Up` / `VirtualKey.Down` are handled only for the slash-command popup; there is no sent-message history.

**Suggested behaviour:** Up on an empty box (or with the caret on the first line) loads the last sent message, repeated Up goes further back, Down moves forward and ends on the empty draft. The popup keeps priority when it is open.

**Related:** #1674 (Enter sends from the multiline composer) is merged, but as far as I can tell it is only in the prerelease v2026.9.9-alpha.3, not in the 2026.9.8-1 release. Observed on 2026.9.8-1.

body:
## Summary
A first-run installation on Windows ARM64 took about 44 minutes across the native Gateway and Local AI setup stages. Long waits and unclear stage completion make it difficult to tell whether setup is progressing or stalled.

## Environment and scope
- Lenovo Yoga 9 2-in-1 16N1X11 (NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X), Windows ARM64
- Windows 11 Pro 26H1, build 28000.3231
- OpenClaw Companion v2026.9.9-alpha.36 (ARM64)
- Native Windows Gateway, followed by recommended Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (UD-Q4_K_S) Local AI model

## Observed timing
- Native Gateway: 23m 46s from WinGet invocation at 15:46:48 to Gateway agent ready at 16:10:34. This includes a five-minute wizard timeout, ongoing Store deployment, waiting, and a setup retry; it is not Gateway process startup time alone.
- Local AI: approximately 20m 13s, from a model-confirmation screenshot at 16:36:56 to a ready-screen snapshot at 16:57:09. This is an upper bound because the exact confirmation click was not logged. The interval includes runtime/model download or verification, model startup, Gateway configuration, and a response check.
- The measured windows sum to roughly 44 minutes. The gap between them is excluded; this was not a continuous unattended benchmark. Network throughput and a second-device baseline were not measured.

## Expected
Make long-running setup stages and their progress clear, so users can distinguish continued work from a stall. Handle slow Store deployment without ending Gateway setup prematurely.

## Actual
On this first-run installation, the Gateway stage took 23m 46s and the Local AI stage took about 20m. The Store installation continued after the setup wizard timed out, requiring a manual retry. This is an observation from one machine, not an established version regression.

OpenClaw Companion v2026.9.9-alpha.36 can disable the “Install a local native gateway” option while presenting an Insider build requirement that is already satisfied by the current Windows build. The message does not identify the failed capability check or provide useful remediation.

## Environment

After Windows updated to build 28000.3231, the option became enabled; the reason for the change is unknown.

Internal tracking: [NVBug 6941780](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6941780).

title: [Windows ARM64] Companion gives misleading build guidance when Native Gateway capability check fails

body:
## Summary
On first-run native Gateway setup, Companion can time out waiting for the Microsoft Store Gateway package while Store deployment continues in the background. The user must wait for deployment and retry setup.

## Environment
- Lenovo Yoga 9 2-in-1 16N1X11 (NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X), Windows ARM64
- Windows 11 Pro 26H1, build 28000.3231 (Insider Beta)
- OpenClaw Companion v2026.9.9-alpha.36 (ARM64)
- Gateway MSIX package 2026.9.900.0

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start Companion with the current-user Gateway package absent.
2. Select native Gateway setup.
3. Let the Microsoft Store download/deploy take longer than the wizard's package acquisition deadline.

## Expected
Setup should remain active with useful progress while Store is making progress, or detect the package and resume when deployment completes.

## Actual
“Install or verify Gateway package” changed to Needs attention with a timeout message, even though Store deployment continued. WinGet started Store execution at 15:46:59; AppX registered the preferred ARM64 package at 15:53:55; Store reported 52% at 15:59:47 and Completed at 16:02:47. The package became installed and aliases available by 16:04. Setup required a retry.

This is one observed first-install attempt. The separate Gateway listener timeout is tracked separately.

Internal tracking: [NVBug 6941836](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6941836).

**Result: the cold Store install path works on current main, but this run does not reproduce the slow (>5 min) Store deployment, so the fix itself is not yet proven. Keep open pending a slow cold-Store retest.**

### Setup
- Code: `main` at `7967d509`, which contains the #1750 merge `64357496` (first release tag with the fix: `v2026.10.9-alpha.12`).
- Machine: Windows 11, x64, build 26100, WinGet v1.29.380.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Effective acquisition deadline | 30 min (`DefaultTimeout`), no `OPENCLAW_SETUP_PACKAGE_ACQUISITION_TIMEOUT` override |
| WinGet install from msstore | exit 0 after **51 s** |
| Registration verification | passed immediately |
| Package | `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClawGateway_rfcbke2p71se2` **2026.10.900.0**, `openclaw.exe` and `clawctl.exe` aliases present |
| Outcome | **SUCCESS in 51 s**, no timeout, no retry |

### What this does and does not prove
- Proves: the current-main install and verify path works end to end against the real Store, and the 30-minute budget is the effective deadline.
- Does not prove: behavior when a cold Store deployment outlives the old 5-minute bound (the original report took about 16 minutes on N1x ARM64). Retest on the original N1x ARM64 machine (or any host where the Store download is slow) with Companion `v2026.10.9-alpha.12` or later, starting without the Gateway package. body:
## Summary
Windows Companion browser control rejects a native Microsoft Store Gateway connection with a local listener ownership verification error. The documented native browser bootstrap helper is also unavailable in the inspected installation.

## Environment
- Windows 11 x64
- Microsoft Store Gateway 2026.9.900.0, running in an isolated Windows account
- Chrome running in the interactive user account
- Windows Companion 2026.9.8-1

## Steps to reproduce
1. Connect Windows Companion to the Gateway.
2. Enable Browser control.
3. Approve the sole requested additions: `browser` and `browser.proxy`.
4. Request node browser status.

## Actual result
Browser control fails with:

```text
Browser control authentication was blocked because the local listener owner could not be verified.
```

The node is paired and connected, and the requested browser capability is approved, but the error persists.

## Expected result
A supported, secure connection from the native Store Gateway to Chrome in the interactive user account, or clear guidance identifying the required component and its official installation route.

## Findings
- The ownership-verification callback in tagged `App.xaml.cs` permits an owned SSH or managed WSL route, but appears to have no native Store Gateway branch: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.9.8-1/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs#L2393-L2428
- Related capability implementation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.9.8-1/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Capabilities/BrowserProxyCapability.cs
- The exact alpha5 source inspected appears to retain the same limitation. Alpha5 was **not installed or tested**; this is a source inspection observation only.
- `OpenClaw.BrowserBootstrap.exe` was absent from the installed Gateway package file inventory. The expected `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\tools\browser-bootstrap` folder was also absent in the interactive user account.
- The documentation describes a native helper route: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/chrome-extension
- No security verification was bypassed and no credentials were copied between accounts.

## Questions
1. Is this native Store Gateway / separate interactive-user Chrome topology supported?
2. Where is the official compatible browser bootstrap helper distributed, and how should it be installed?
3. Is a browser-only connection in the interactive user account supported without migrating the Gateway out of its isolated account?

body:
## Summary
OpenClaw Companion (Windows Hub) becomes unresponsive ("not responding") right after connecting to a **remote** Gateway, and stays that way across restarts. While it is hung, tray menu items such as **Companion Settings…** do nothing, so node mode cannot be configured or repaired from the UI.

## Environment
- Windows Hub: 2026.9.8-1 (x64, Windows 11)
- Gateway: 2026.9.7 on macOS, protocol 4, auth mode token
- Connection: remote Gateway over Tailscale Serve (`wss://<host>.ts.net`, tailnet-only, valid Let's Encrypt cert), paired with a setup code from `openclaw qr --setup-code-only --url wss://…`
- Setup choices: Advanced → existing Gateway, capabilities preset **Balanced**, model "Current model"

## Timeline (from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\Logs\diagnostics.jsonl` + Gateway log)
1. 12:26 `app.start nodeMode=false` → Connected, healthy. Operator device pairing approved on the Gateway (`openclaw devices approve`). Setup wizard completes ("Your AI is ready").
2. 12:39 `app.start nodeMode=true` (turned on by the Balanced preset). Node client `Windows Node (BSH-OFFICE) node v2026.9.8-1 role=node auth=bootstrap-token` is rejected by the Gateway every reconnect: `reason=bootstrap_token_invalid` (the setup code had already been redeemed by the operator connection). App becomes "not responding".
3. User ends the task and reopens: still hung.
4. `nodeMode` set to `false` by hand in `%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\settings.json`, app reopened at 13:07: the node retries stop, and the operator connection succeeds (`health`, `agents.list`, `node.list` OK). `chat.history` returns in about 1.35 s for a very large, long-running main session (months of messages and tool output). Two `users.self` calls fail with `FORBIDDEN … requires an authenticated user` on every connect. The UI is still frozen, and Companion Settings does nothing.

## Expected
- The app stays responsive when node bootstrap auth fails. It should show a pairing or repair prompt instead of hanging.
- The setup wizard should not reuse an already-redeemed setup code for node mode. Either mint or request a node credential, or tell the user a second code is needed.
- Loading a very large chat history should not block the UI thread. Paginate, or lazy-load the history.
- A failing `users.self` (FORBIDDEN) should not block startup.

## Workaround in use
The browser Control UI works over the same Tailscale Serve URL. Node mode is not usable.

Happy to provide more logs, or test a build.

**Environment**
- Windows Companion: Microsoft Store build 2026.10.401 (x64, Windows 11). Reproduced first on 2026.9.8-1 (Inno build).
- Gateway: 2026.10.4 (Docker, Linux arm64), protocol 4, token auth.
- Connection: remote, `wss://` through a TLS reverse proxy (nginx, WebSocket upgrade forwarded).

**1. Setup code is burned by the operator connection**
On 2026.10.4 the gateway pairs a setup-code connection silently only when it is a mobile node (`role=node`, `client.mode=node`; `isMobileNodeBootstrapConnect` in the gateway's message handler). The Companion connects first as `role=operator`, `clientId=cli`, `mode=cli` with the bootstrap token. That connection gets `pairing-required`, and the code is consumed. After `openclaw devices approve` it keeps retrying with the same code, gets `bootstrap_token_invalid`, and generates a new device identity on each fresh setup attempt.
Workaround: skip the setup code and enter the gateway URL and the shared gateway token by hand. Then approve the pending request once. The node role upgrade was auto-approved after that.

**2. The freeze is the native chat view, not history size and not node mode**
- Windows logs `AppHangB1` / `MoAppHang`. There is no exception in `openclaw-tray.log`.
- The last tray log lines before every hang are `Sending frame: chat.history` and `Wizard response payload kind=Object len=20102`. The default thread (`agent:main:main`) is small here: 44 transcript events, about 20 KB of history. So this is not only a "very large history" problem.
- Setting `"EnableNodeMode": false` in `%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\settings.json` did **not** stop the hang.
- The connection is healthy the whole time: Connected within about 1 s on every start, and the node is paired and connected.
- `users.self` -> `FORBIDDEN` is logged on every connect, but it falls back cleanly ("using owner fallback"). It is not the cause.

**Workaround that works:** set `"UseLegacyWebChat": true` in `%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\settings.json`, with the app fully closed. After that the Companion opens normally, chat works, and the node connects with its canvas/tts/stt commands.

This points at the native chat rendering path (see also #1167, #1568), not at pairing or history size.

Please add updated OpenClaw Windows details or it will be closed.

Environment

OpenClaw Companion (Tray) 2026.9.8-1, Windows 10/11 x64
Gateway 2026.9.9, packaged install (MSIX), managed by clawctl (OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external), listening on 127.0.0.1:57367, gateway.auth.mode: token
The gateway process runs under Windows user A. The Companion app runs under Windows user B, on the same PC.

What happens

“Connect to an existing gateway” with address ws://127.0.0.1:57367 and the shared token shows: “gateway connection check failed.”
The gateway log shows the app is reached and rejected: client=OpenClaw Windows Tray cli v2026.9.8-1 role=operator auth=token device=yes reason=token_mismatch.
openclaw gateway status --require-rpc --token <token from gateway config> succeeds with the same token. A deliberately wrong token fails. So the token is valid.
Using a setup code from openclaw qr --setup-code-only --url ws://127.0.0.1:57367 makes the app show: “Invalid base64: The input is not a valid Base-64 string as it contains a non-base 64 character, more than two padding characters, or an illegal character among the padding characters.”
openclaw devices list and openclaw nodes pending show nothing pending. A stale Tray entry was removed. The app’s Local and Roaming data folders were reset.

Expected
The app connects with the gateway’s shared token, or with a setup code, and shows a pairing request if needed.

Questions

Does the app send a token from a different source than the one typed into the field?
Does the setup code field expect a different encoding than the output of openclaw qr --setup-code-only?
Does running the gateway and the app under different Windows users break the connection check?

body:
# [Feature Request] Add Fish Audio TTS provider to Windows Hub voice settings

## Summary

Please add **Fish Audio** as a TTS provider option in Windows Hub's voice/settings UI, alongside the current local providers (Windows SAPI, ElevenLabs, MiniMax, Piper).

## Motivation

Fish Audio runs a genuinely free API tier that is materially better than the alternatives for hobbyist/personal-assistant use:

- **`s2.1-pro-free`** — the same state-of-the-art S2.1 Pro model as the paid tier, **no hard usage cap** (Fair Use Policy only), 83 languages including Malay. Free access is documented through **2026-11-30** (https://fish.audio/blog/s2-1-pro-free-api/).
- ElevenLabs' free tier is effectively a trial (10k credits/month); OpenAI and Gemini TTS have no free tier at all.
- Fish has a large public voice library plus voice cloning from a reference clip — useful for personalized assistant voices.

On the Gateway side this is already well-supported: `talk.catalog` reports `fish-audio` as `configured: true` (via the speech-provider plugin), so the Gateway can already synthesize with Fish today. Only the Hub app's own local voice dropdown is missing it.

## Current state (verified 2026-10-11, Hub v2026.9.8.0)

- Hub binaries (`OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.dll`, `OpenClaw.Shared.dll`, `OpenClawTray.FunctionalUI.dll`, `OpenClaw.Connection.dll`) contain zero references to Fish: keyword scan returns `fish=0`, vs `piper=23–33`, `minimax=13–14`, `elevenlabs=10`.
- App settings (`%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\settings.json`) carry keys only for the existing four providers (`TtsWindowsVoiceId`, `TtsElevenLabs*`, `TtsMiniMax*`, `TtsPiper*`).
- The upstream `openclaw` repo has the provider (extensions/fish-audio-speech and community plugin @conan-scott/openclaw-fish-audio); `openclaw-windows-node` has none.

## Suggested implementation

Follow the existing per-provider settings convention. Suggested keys (naming aligned with current schema):

```jsonc
{
  "TtsProvider": "fish-audio",
  "TtsFishApiKey": "<dpapi-protected>",      // from https://fish.audio/app/api-keys/
  "TtsFishVoiceId": "<reference-id>",         // Fish voice model id; clone or public library
  "TtsFishModel": "s2.1-pro-free",            // s2.1-pro-free | s2-pro | s1
  "TtsFishLatency": "balanced"                // normal | balanced | low
}
```

API contract (verified working today against `https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts`):

```http
POST /v1/tts HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <api-key>
Content-Type: application/json
model: s2.1-pro-free          <-- NOTE: model is an HTTP HEADER, not a body field

{ "text": "...", "reference_id": "<voice-id>", "format": "mp3", "latency": "balanced" }
```

Response is raw audio bytes (mp3/opus). One authenticated probe today: `200 OK`, ~72 KB MP3 for a short Malay sentence, ~3.4 s round-trip through the OpenClaw pipeline. Without the `model` header the API falls back to a paid model and returns `402 Insufficient API credit` — worth inheriting in a comment so future maintainers don't lose an afternoon to it.

Reference implementation of the request/response handling already exists in the Gateway plugin (`openclaw/extensions/fish-audio-speech/tts.ts` + community `@conan-scott/openclaw-fish-audio`), including voice listing (`GET /model?type=tts&self=true`), latency/format handling and error mapping (401 key, 402 credit).

## Alternative / bigger win: Gateway-provided voice

Independent of adding a per-provider client, Hub could offer a **"Gateway (delegated)"** voice option that routes `talk.speak`/`tts.speak` through the connected Gateway's active speech provider. Because the Hub already declares Talk capability and `talk.catalog` advertises every Gateway-provider's readiness, that single option would give Hub users access to **every** Gateway TTS provider (Fish, ElevenLabs, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, …) with no per-provider Windows code, and it stays in sync automatically. Per-provider local settings could remain for the offline/local-only case.

## Use case

Malaysian user running a personal-assistant setup (voice replies + voice notes) who wants natural-sounding Malay output at zero recurring cost. Fish's free tier covers this today; ElevenLabs/MiniMax would require paid credits or accept noticeably worse prosody for `ms-MY`.

Happy to test a build and provide probe scripts — the direct-API verification script used for the evidence above is at `C:\Users\User\.openclaw\workspace\scripts\fish-header-test.cjs` if a reference helps.

# Native Gateway: browser status/profiles blocked by listener ownership verification

## Environment

- Windows Companion: v2026.9.8-1, matching the latest official GitHub release checked today.
- Gateway CLI: v2026.9.9.
- Local Native Gateway using the packaged runtime.
- The paired Windows Node is connected and advertises browser capability and browser.proxy.

## Reproduction and observed result

The main agent used the official browser tool to request status and profiles on the connected Windows Node. Both requests failed with:

> Browser control authentication was blocked because the local listener owner could not be verified.

No browser launch or Chrome attachment occurred. The intended Gemini test was never sent. This report contains no credentials, personal paths, account identifiers, or raw diagnostic logs.

## Investigation

The error is produced by BrowserProxyCapability before sending authentication to the local browser control service.

In the installed release's browserControlAuthorization callback, I found checks for an SSH-owned listener and an application-managed local WSL Gateway. I did not find a Native Gateway runtime ownership branch in that callback. The active configuration has a Native package/runtime contract, no SSH configuration, and no setup-managed WSL name.

This suggests a mismatch between the Native Gateway configuration and the ownership-validation path. It is a hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause: I have not determined which internal validation condition returns false.

## Expected behavior and request

Please confirm whether browser.proxy ownership validation is supported for this Native Gateway configuration in the current release, and whether there is a supported fix or configuration procedure.

The ownership check has not been disabled, and no authentication data or browser profiles have been copied. I am looking for a supported solution that preserves the security checks.

## References

- [BrowserProxyCapability in the installed release](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.9.8-1/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Capabilities/BrowserProxyCapability.cs#L73-L80)
- [Browser authorization callback in the installed release](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.9.8-1/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs#L2220-L2254)
- [Gateway node browser routing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.9/docs/tools/browser/remote.md#node-browser-proxy-zero-config-default)

## Problem

OpenClaw Companion on Windows cannot connect to the saved “Native Gateway”, so I cannot chat through the desktop app.

The error says that the installed Gateway MSIX does not expose Companion’s isolated-session contract. It asks me to update the Gateway MSIX and retry setup, and says credentials were not sent.

- Uninstalled OpenClaw Companion while keeping the local Gateway and its data.

- Retried Connect and Save & connect.
- Tried Open dashboard.

The connection form shows “Gateway reachable”, but connecting still produces the same error. Open dashboard also fails and asks me to check the verified gateway connection.

## Expected result

Companion should connect and allow me to chat with my existing agent.

## Request

Which Gateway MSIX and Companion versions are compatible with this isolated-session contract? Please provide a supported repair or upgrade procedure that preserves existing conversations and settings.

I have not removed or reset the Gateway.

- Companion (Microsoft Store): `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw` 2026.10.401.0
- Separately installed native Gateway MSIX: `OpenClaw.Gateway` 2026.10.400.0
- Native isolated-session setup; Gateway port 18789

**Working**
- `clawctl gateway-service start --json` reports Gateway running and listening on port 18789.
- `clawctl open` opens a functioning browser Control UI, including agent chat.
- OpenAI Codex OAuth onboarding completed.
- `clawctl companion prepare --port 18789` succeeds.
- `openclaw devices list` shows paired Windows Tray and TUI devices.

**Failing**
- Windows Companion remains disconnected: “The native Gateway could not start or verify its owned endpoint. Check the manually installed MSIX and retry. Credentials were not sent.”
- Connection timeline: “Blocked strong credential before managed-local endpoint ownership was proven” and “The managed gateway address is owned by an unverified process. OpenClaw did not send the shared or bootstrap token.”
- Diagnostic log: `Local AI ownership discovery is unavailable (InvalidOperationException)`.
- Native HTTP credential handoff reports `UnknownListener`.
- Companion persists an old “last successful” Gateway URL at `ws://127.0.0.1:63015/` (no listener there), while the actual Gateway runs on 18789. Manually targeting 18789 has not resolved ownership verification.
- An earlier direct connection to 18789 reached the challenge but failed `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH`; the Tray device was subsequently paired, but the ownership failure persisted.
- Setup recovery also reports that original Gateway ownership/configuration could not be checked.

A clean reinstall and fresh isolated-session setup have already been attempted. Windows build exceeds the documented minimum. No ownership/security check has been bypassed.

Could maintainers confirm whether Companion 2026.10.401.0 and the separately installed `OpenClaw.Gateway` 2026.10.400.0 package are expected to interoperate, and suggest a **non-destructive** diagnostic/recovery procedure for the ownership handshake? Sanitised diagnostics can be provided on request.

Additional reproduction with a specific multi-listener cause on the official Windows Gateway release. This may explain some reports in this thread; it does not establish that every report has the same cause.

### Environment observed October 20, 2026

- Windows 11 x64, build 26300.9711.
- Store Companion `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw` 2026.10.401.0; executable reports `2026.10.4-alpha.5`, commit `c2ce4f50eb6313121ffb385e086cf4c4ba7b982b`.
- Store Gateway `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClawGateway` 2026.10.400.0, packaging commit `19d7cc0aab651c4d940517abcdaeeac1987a06d0`.
- Bundled OpenClaw 2026.10.4, commit `383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af`.
- One supported Gateway package registered during this reproduction. Gateway configured on loopback port 61393; its launcher configuration explicitly pins that same port.

### Reproduction and observed results

1. Start the configured native Gateway. The package-qualified `clawctl gateway-service status --json` reports `running`, port 61393 and session/process ownership including a nonzero process sequence number. Companion connects successfully.
2. Run the packaged `openclaw browser status --json`. It reports the managed browser is stopped, but this initializes another loopback listener on 61403 in the same Gateway Node process. Starting a managed browser is not required to trigger this case.
3. Repeat the package-qualified `clawctl gateway-service status --json`. It now returns:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "command": "gateway-service status",
  "gateway": { "state": "running" },
  "integration": { "kind": "isolated-session", "version": 1 }
}
```

Both `gateway.port` and `gateway.ownership` have disappeared while the two Node-owned listeners remain active.

4. Disconnect and reconnect Companion. It displays: “The installed Gateway MSIX does not expose Companion's isolated-session contract.” Credentials are withheld.
5. A supported Gateway restart clears the auxiliary listener and allows Companion to connect again. The failure returns when browser functionality initializes the extra listener. Restarting is therefore temporary recovery.

### Source path matching the observations

In [the installed Gateway source, Program.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging/blob/19d7cc0aab651c4d940517abcdaeeac1987a06d0/src/OpenClaw.Launcher/Program.cs#L986), the `GatewayStatus` handler selects a port only when `ObservedPorts` has exactly one entry. It discards an explicitly pinned Gateway port even when that port is among the freshly observed listeners.

[ClawCtlJson.FromOwnership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging/blob/19d7cc0aab651c4d940517abcdaeeac1987a06d0/src/OpenClaw.Launcher/ClawCtlJson.cs#L314) requires the selected port before serializing ownership. [Companion's parser](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/c2ce4f50eb6313121ffb385e086cf4c4ba7b982b/src/OpenClaw.Connection/NativeGateway/NativeGatewayPackageClient.cs) requires that port for a running Gateway and emits the generic contract error when it is missing.

The same `Count: 1` status selection was still present in upstream main when checked for this report. The observed integration remains version 1; no contract-version edit or ownership bypass is needed to reproduce this failure.

### Local repair deployed and verified — October 20 update

A local Gateway source change routes status and dashboard endpoint selection through an observed-port selector: select the configured port only when it is among the fresh observations; leave genuinely ambiguous unpinned listeners unresolved. Session identity, listener attribution and process-sequence checks remain enforced. Companion's generic error wording has not been changed; distinguishing missing endpoint information from an unsupported contract remains a suggested Companion improvement.

Validation now completed:

- Regression cases exercise the actual status-result mapping and JSON serializer. Multiple-listener cases fail with the original selector and pass with the repair. All 35 targeted status/address/ownership/dashboard tests and the canonical Release analysis/formatting gate pass.
- All 30 NativeAOT CLI scenarios pass. The production launcher and session helper compiled successfully.
- Full patched suite: 1,306 passed, 12 failed. The unmodified baseline has the exact same 12 failures: 11 symlink-privilege failures before Developer Mode was enabled, and one Windows PowerShell fixture blocked by execution policy. Tests and security policies were not weakened; the full suite was not rerun after enabling Developer Mode.
- Deployed a separate local Developer Mode Gateway package, `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClawGateway-owned-port` version `0.1.2484.14125`, using the repository's documented side-by-side patch workflow. The application payload remains the same Store payload/version/commit listed above. This is a local development build, not a Store-signed or officially released fix.
- With relay 61403 and managed-browser CDP 61404 active, status retained Gateway port 61393 and fresh ownership evidence for all three listeners. Companion disconnect/reconnect succeeded under this formerly failing condition.
- Companion opened the authenticated dashboard and displayed restored history. Qwen3.5 9B message exchanges passed through the patched Gateway, including a message sent inside Companion after a full Companion process restart through Windows app activation with browser listeners still active.
- After a supported Gateway restart, browser listeners were recreated; Companion was reconnected and reopened, and another message sent inside Companion received the expected response. This verifies fresh-process ownership rather than relying on a healthy readiness endpoint alone.
- Migration used verified full backups and a separate isolated profile. All 894 restored state files were hash-verified, five SQLite databases passed integrity checks, and configuration values were preserved except three absolute paths updated for the new profile. The existing Companion device key was verified unchanged. The Store Gateway and recovered data remain available for rollback; only the patch is active on the configured port.

### Separate restart/retry limitation remains

Restarting Gateway while Companion stays open exposed a separate recovery issue. Companion retried about one second later while Gateway was still starting, then stopped retrying after reporting that the package-managed Gateway was not running on its selected port. Once Gateway was ready, clicking Connect restored native connectivity, but the already-open embedded web chat remained blank until Companion was reopened. Reopening Companion against the ready patched Gateway succeeded with all browser listeners active. Automatic recovery across that restart gap is **not** claimed fixed by the endpoint-selection patch.

Tests used Companion's web-chat preference, which avoids a separately observed native WinUI layout-cycle crash. The offending native control has not been established or repaired.

This confirms a local repair for this reproduced multi-listener case. It does not establish that the original poster or every other reporter has the same cause, and it does not establish availability of an official released repair.

Could the Windows Gateway packaging maintainers confirm this endpoint-selection defect and provide a released repair preserving existing data and credential protections? The producer is in `openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging`; this comment supplies the reproducer missing from the existing Companion symptom report.

No credentials, device keys, user/account identifiers, private profile paths, conversation content, raw logs, crash dumps or diagnostic attachments are included. Loopback ports and public software versions/source references are retained to make the reproduction useful.

**Resolved on my installation — follow-up to [my earlier reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1691#issuecomment-6248926574).**

The Windows desktop app now connects to the native Gateway, and an end-to-end chat message was successfully sent and answered through it.

**What fixed this particular case (no reinstall, package change, data reset, or ownership-check bypass):**

1. `clawctl gateway-service status --json` confirmed the current native Gateway was running on **127.0.0.1:18789**, with valid-looking `gateway.ownership` data and `integration.kind=isolated-session`, version 1. The desktop app's saved “Native Gateway” entry still pointed at **ws://127.0.0.1:63015**.
2. Removed that obsolete *saved connection* through the desktop app (not the Gateway installation/data), then used **Connect to an existing Gateway → Direct via URL and token**, targeting **ws://127.0.0.1:18789**.
3. The first attempt reached the Gateway and received **AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH**. The saved shared token was not the current Gateway's token. From the isolated environment, retrieved the current token with `clawctl pwsh` followed by `openclaw gateway auth-token --show`, and used it in the connection form.
4. A subsequent attempt showed **Transport error**. Checking `clawctl gateway-service status --json` showed `gateway.state=stopped`, with the supervisor reporting exit code 1. `clawctl gateway-service start --json`, followed by status verification, restored the Gateway on port 18789.
5. Retrying **Save & Connect** with the current token then produced **Gateway pairing approval required**, rather than an ownership or token error. `clawctl pwsh --command "openclaw devices list"` showed one pending **OpenClaw Windows Tray** pairing request. Approved that specific request using `clawctl pwsh --command "openclaw devices approve <pending-request-id>"`.
6. After a short delay, the desktop app showed **Connected**. An actual chat exchange in the desktop app succeeded, with the agent confirming the message had arrived through the Gateway.

**Environment:** Windows 10.0.26300.0; desktop `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw` 2026.10.401.0; separately installed native Gateway `OpenClaw.Gateway` 2026.10.400.0.

**Scope/qualification:** This is a verified recovery for my case, not evidence that all reports here share the same cause. The initial ownership-verification message was real, but the working recovery path involved correcting a stale saved endpoint, using the current Gateway auth token, ensuring the Gateway was running, and explicitly approving the new device pairing. The Gateway's transient exit-code-1 stop was not root-caused. The desktop app's tendency to repopulate the obsolete port/token after removing the saved connection may still merit investigation.

This issue has been automatically marked as stale due to inactivity.
Please add updated OpenClaw Windows details or it will be closed.

Same symptom here, with an additional data point that matches the analysis above (missing `gateway.port` in `clawctl status`).

**Environment**
- Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, Gateway MSIX `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClawGateway 2026.11.100.0` (Microsoft Store), payload 2026.11.1
- Companion tried in two builds, same result: Inno `2026.11.1` and Store `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw 2026.11.102.0` (clean migration, no legacy install left)
- Gateway runs in the isolated session (agent user), Companion runs in the human user session

**Error shown in Companion (both builds)**
> The installed Gateway MSIX does not expose Companion's isolated-session contract. Update the Gateway MSIX, then retry setup. Credentials were not sent.

Earlier Inno build also logged: `Native Gateway HTTP credential handoff denied: UnknownListener`.

**What the package reports (values redacted)**
- `clawctl status --json` and `clawctl gateway-service status --json`: `ok: true`, `gateway.state: "running"`, `gateway.launch.version: 1`, `integration: { kind: "isolated-session", version: 1, gatewayLaunch: { version: 1 } }`. There is **no `gateway.port` and no ownership block** in the `gateway` object.
- `clawctl companion prepare --check --json`: returns `companion.port: 50071` and a token, so the Gateway does listen on 50071 and the port is known to the package.
- The Gateway itself works: CLI, cron and agent runs all succeed against it.

So the integration metadata is valid but the running status has no selected port, which fits the "exactly one observed listener" selection and the generic missing-contract message described in #2020. I could not check how many listeners the isolated session has, since they are not visible from the human account.

**Not found**: no Store update available (winget/Store show nothing newer), so "update the Gateway MSIX" has no way forward here.

Happy to run any diagnostic you want (e.g. `clawctl collect-logs`) and report redacted output.

title: [Bug] Companion cannot connect: Gateway MSIX missing isolated-session contract

body:
## Summary

Windows Hub intermittently loses its Gateway connections, including while the agent is idle. One node-exec request failed during `system.run.prepare` despite the Hub logging local completion and an `ok=True` result send attempt. Root cause is unresolved; the report distinguishes observed failures from source-level hypotheses.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, build 26300.
- Hub 2026.9.8-1, installed product revision `2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114`.
- Installed self-contained runtime configuration: .NET / WindowsDesktop 10.0.12.
- Gateway 2026.9.9 (`bcfc888`), Node 24.19.0, Ubuntu-26.04 in WSL2 with mirrored networking.
- Ordinary Gateway listener is loopback-only. No externally managed reverse proxy targets it. `gateway.roles` is absent and `gateway.trustedProxies` is empty.
- Three Windows nodes exist. The original command explicitly targeted the Hub; later generic node-mode close records cannot all be assigned to it.

## Observed reproduction

This is an intermittent live-installation observation, not a deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Connect the Windows Hub operator and node roles to the WSL Gateway.
2. From a Main agent session, request a harmless echo through node exec, explicitly targeting the Hub with a Windows working directory and a 20-second tool timeout.
3. Observe the request fail after approximately 5.8 seconds with `DISCONNECTED: node disconnected (system.run.prepare)`, without stdout or exit status.
4. Leave the agent idle. Automatic reconnects and premature closures also occur without another command.

Expected: prepare returns to the Gateway and an ordinary harmless command completes, or transport failure is reported accurately. Actual: result delivery is unconfirmed and sockets reconnect repeatedly.

## Sanitized timeline, 2026-10-09 (BST, UTC+1)

Original request:

| Time | Hub observation |
| --- | --- |
| 15:53:10.328 | Prepare handled locally |
| 15:53:10.332 | Invoke-result send logged with `ok=True` |
| 15:53:10.336 | Local prepare invocation completed |
| 15:53:12.458 | `Connection closed prematurely` |
| 15:53:12.459 | Node disconnected |
| 15:53:15.998 | Node registered again |

A later three-minute stock verbose-WebSocket observation, with no command canary, recorded:

| Time | Connection prefix | Client mode | Close code | Cause | Ping write | Last pong age (ms) | Buffered bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16:33:51.942 | d0aee6ef | cli | 1006 | heartbeat-timeout | completed | 44710.8 | 0 |
| 16:34:23.160 | 8f0379a3 | node | 1006 | heartbeat-timeout | completed | 39671.8 | 0 |

Hub independently logged premature closure at exactly 16:33:51.942. That is strong correlation, not definitive process attribution: the Hub operator declares `cli/cli`, while its node declares `node-host/node`. The second record has not been assigned to a particular Windows node. The original prepare failure has no retained matching Gateway close-cause record.

Completed ping writes and zero buffered output do not prove peer receipt. A transient Gateway event-loop delay was observed near the original failure, but later idle disconnects mean it is not established as the sole cause. HTTP health checks returned 200 after restoration; the restored Gateway process stayed active with no automatic restarts, and the Hub process remained alive. Diagnostic logging was restored to normal afterward. These checks do not establish continuous uptime or a functioning node-exec route.

## Exact-revision source findings, not a root-cause claim

- [WebSocketClientBase.cs:472 onward](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114/src/OpenClaw.Shared/WebSocketClientBase.cs#L472) awaits message processing between receives. A blocking handler/subscriber could delay control-frame processing, but no such runtime stall has been demonstrated.
- Accepted node capabilities already run off the receive loop through `Task.Run`: [WindowsNodeClient.cs:630](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114/src/OpenClaw.Shared/WindowsNodeClient.cs#L630). The slow-capability test at [WindowsNodeClientTests.cs:3655](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114/tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/WindowsNodeClientTests.cs#L3655) exercises message dispatch, not wire-level heartbeat behavior; it was inspected, not run here.
- The `ok=True` result log precedes the socket write: [WindowsNodeClient.cs:644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114/src/OpenClaw.Shared/WindowsNodeClient.cs#L644). The untracked [SendRawAsync helper, WebSocketClientBase.cs:744](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114/src/OpenClaw.Shared/WebSocketClientBase.cs#L744) can return without sending on a closed socket. Thus local completion does not establish Gateway receipt.
- The premature-close warning at [WebSocketClientBase.cs:555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114/src/OpenClaw.Shared/WebSocketClientBase.cs#L555) has no role or connection-generation label, limiting attribution.
- [Microsoft guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/networking/websockets) and the [.NET 10.0.12 implementation](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/v10.0.12/src/libraries/System.Net.WebSockets/src/System/Net/WebSockets/ManagedWebSocket.cs) confirm automatic protocol PONG handling during receive. Adding an application-level JSON ping handler is not an established fix.

## Related reports and request

This differs from #1190, where MXC executes successfully but exceeds an approximately 30-second RPC limit. This failure happened during prepare, with disconnection after approximately 5.8 seconds and no process-execution receipt. It also differs from #1574, which concerns reconnects during Windows session teardown; no shutdown was in progress here.

Is there a released, supported repair matching this behavior? Otherwise, what bounded role/generation-specific diagnostic would distinguish missed protocol PONG processing from transport loss and attribute operator versus node closures? No permission expansion, timeout workaround, network-mode change, or unmerged patch has been applied. No raw traffic, session content, credentials, or personal paths are included.

title: [Bug] Hub 2026.9.8-1: premature WebSocket closures and lost system.run.prepare result with WSL Gateway

body:
## Summary
Every exec with host=node fails on the Windows node with:
Invalid system.run request: custom-env-not-supported

The gateway attaches OPENCLAW_CHANNEL_CONTEXT to every system.run.prepare request, and the node rejects it within ~1 ms, before sandbox or folder policy is evaluated. Even `hostname` fails, so the node cannot run any command.

## Versions
- Companion: v2026.9.8-1 (build 07/10/2026, stable channel, install type shown as "Unpackaged (developer)")
- Gateway: 2026.9.8 (app-owned local WSL gateway)
- Windows 11 10.0.26300.0, x64
- Node Sandbox: on (MXC), custom folder grants configured

## Steps to reproduce
1. Pair the Companion node with the local WSL gateway; Node mode and Run system tools on.
2. In chat: "Run one command on the Windows node: hostname".

## Log (openclaw-tray.log, IDs redacted)
[2026-10-09 14:29:27.407] [DEBUG] [NODE RX] {"type":"event","event":"node.invoke.request","payload":{"command":"system.run.prepare","paramsJSON":"{\"command\":[\"cmd.exe\",\"/d\",\"/s\",\"/c\",\"hostname\"],\"security\":\"full\",\"ask\":\"off\",\"rawCommand\":\"hostname\",\"env\":{\"OPENCLAW_CHANNEL_CONTEXT\":\"{\\\"sender\\\":{\\\"id\\\":\\\"cli\\\"}}\"},\"agentId\":\"main\"}","timeoutMs":30000}}
[2026-10-09 14:29:27.408] [INFO] [NODE] Invoking command: system.run.prepare
[2026-10-09 14:29:27.409] [INFO] [NODE] Sending invoke result: ok=False
[2026-10-09 14:29:27.409] [INFO] [ActivityStream] Item added: [node.invoke] node.invoke failed: system.run.prepare

## Expected
Either the node accepts or strips the gateway-injected OPENCLAW_CHANNEL_CONTEXT, or the gateway omits it for Windows nodes that do not support custom env.

body:
### Summary
Clicking the paperclip (attach) button in the chat composer makes the Windows app exit immediately (fail-fast: no error dialog, no managed exception). Still reproducible after upgrading to v2026.9.8-1 (previously reproduced on 2026.9.4.0).

### Environment
- App: OpenClaw Tray / Windows Companion (WinUI) — OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe
- App version: v2026.9.8-1 (installed via OpenClawCompanion-Setup-x64.exe, release tag v2026.9.8-1)
  - Also reproduced on 2026.9.4.0 (product 2026.9.4+3c43751b)
- OS: Windows 11 (faulting module ntdll.dll 10.0.26100.9549)
- Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (protocol 4), remote gateway

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open the app's Chat page, connected to a gateway.
2. Click the paperclip / attach button in the composer.
3. The whole app exits instantly — no dialog appears.

Reproduced 3/3 times on 2026-09-26 (20:12:35, 20:13:22, 20:30:17 local) and again after updating to v2026.9.8-1 on 2026-10-08.

### Expected
The native file picker opens and the selected file is staged in the composer.

### Actual
The process dies immediately.

### Evidence
- openclaw-tray.log: the last line before each crash is
  `[INFO] [ChatPage] OnAttachClicked invoked`
  and the next launch logs `[ERROR] Previous session did not exit cleanly`.
- Windows Application Error event (identical each time):
  faulting module `ntdll.dll`, exception code `0xc0000409` (fail-fast), faulting offset `0x124406`.
- Crash dumps present: %LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps\OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe.<pid>.dmp
- No managed exception is written to the crash log for these crashes → native fail-fast, consistent with opening the file picker without a valid window handle.

### Workaround
Pasting (Ctrl+V) or dragging the same file into the window works, and the gateway accepts the attachment — only the paperclip path crashes.

### Notes
- Searched the tracker: no existing issue for this crash (keyword OnAttachClicked → 0 hits). Closest are #1621 / #1644 (attachment handling), which are not crashes.
- Happy to provide a crash dump / WER report if useful.

- Address: `0x7ff9d9344406` -> **`ntdll.dll + 0x124406`** (identical to the WER event already

(`clr.dll` / `coreclr.dll` / `mscorlib.ni.dll`), i.e. the fail-fast appears to be raised by the
runtime rather than by a plain native AV inside the picker code.

**Loaded modules: 328.** Framework-dependent .NET/WinUI 3 app (`coreclr.dll`, `hostfxr.dll`,
`Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll`, `Microsoft.WindowsAppRuntime.dll` all loaded from the app folder).

process at crash time** — the classic source of in-process file-picker crashes:

the Microsoft symbol server, and check whether the crash still reproduces with the cloud-sync
shell extensions unregistered / shell extensions disabled. If it does not reproduce without them,
the failing native operation is likely inside a third-party namespace/overlay extension invoked
while the picker enumerates the shell namespace.

body:
## Request

Offer an **opt-in full Control UI mode inside the Windows Companion WebView**, in addition to the current integrated Web UI chat mode. The integrated mode deliberately hides the embedded Control UI's navigation/sidebar in favor of the Companion's native Workspace sidebar. There is currently no user-facing choice to keep the full embedded Control UI.

This corrects the original report: **the native Workspace sidebar is present and functioning**. The missing sidebar is the **web Control UI sidebar inside the embedded WebView**, not `WorkspaceWindow`'s native `NavigationView`. The screenshot supplied by the reporter shows the native agent selector, Home, Sessions, and session rows open beside the embedded web chat; the embedded web sidebar is absent. Session names in that screenshot are private, so it is described here rather than attached unredacted.

## Environment and steps

- Windows Companion/node **2026.9.8-1**; Windows **10.0.26200.9550**
- WSL Gateway CLI **OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)**
- Settings → **Use gateway's web chat interface** enabled (`UseLegacyWebChat`)

1. Open Workspace/Chat with the Web UI setting enabled.
2. Observe that the **native** Workspace sidebar is open and lists sessions.
3. Observe that the embedded **web** Control UI shows chat content but not its own sidebar/navigation.
4. Open the same Gateway Control UI in Opera: its web sidebar is visible.

The reporter previously sometimes saw the embedded web sidebar after navigating from Chat to Connection and back in the old single-window shell. That workaround no longer has the same navigation path now that Settings/Connection is a separate window.

## New functional evidence: removing the injected style reveals the web sidebar

In the embedded WebView's DevTools, the reporter identified and removed the `<style>` element injected by `ChatPage.xaml.cs`. A reproducible console check is:

```js
const injected = [...document.querySelectorAll('style')].filter(
  style => style.textContent.includes('nav, [data-sidebar], .sidebar, aside { display: none !important; }')
);
console.log(`Companion sidebar-hiding styles found: ${injected.length}`);
injected.forEach(style => style.remove());
```

**Observed result:** the matching style was found and removed, and the complete web Control UI sidebar appeared immediately inside the existing Companion WebView. No reload, Gateway/configuration change, or Companion binary modification was needed. This confirms that the sidebar is present and renderable in the current WebView and that the injected style is the immediate cause of its absence. It does **not** yet establish that all Control UI navigation works correctly inside Companion, or that this DevTools change survives reload, navigation, or restart. The console snippet above is a minimal way to reproduce the reporter's style-removal experiment, not a persistent fix.

## Confirmed implementation / why this is an enhancement

- At the installed release, `ChatPage.xaml.cs` lines 997–1026 attach a `WebView2.NavigationCompleted` handler. On successful navigation it injects CSS with `nav, [data-sidebar], .sidebar, aside { display: none !important; }`, accompanied by the explicit comment, “Hide the web Control UI sidebar — Hub NavigationView handles top-level nav.” [Release source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.9.8-1/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/ChatPage.xaml.cs#L997-L1026)
- The Settings toggle describes hosting the Gateway web chat *instead of the native Windows chat experience*, but does not distinguish integrated chat from the full Control UI. [Settings UI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.9.8-1/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/SettingsPage.xaml#L185-L198)
- Git blame/history places the CSS injection before the Workspace/Settings split (it exists in the parent of [#1541](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1541)). Previously, Chat and Connection navigated through the same `HubWindow.ContentFrame`; returning to Chat called `ChatPage.Initialize()`, which re-navigated an initialized WebView. In the current architecture `WorkspaceWindow` owns a retained `ChatPage` and Settings is a separate window. The old round-trip therefore no longer forces the same Chat-page lifecycle. [Pre-split Hub navigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/e00ce903eda5f2c4b2f0b93f139c6f25315773a4/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Windows/HubWindow.xaml.cs) · [Current Workspace host](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.9.8-1/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Windows/WorkspaceWindow.xaml.cs) · [Current window routing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.9.8-1/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/WindowManager.cs)

The source establishes that hiding the embedded web sidebar is **intentional** and is **not a new technical regression**. It does **not** establish why the old round-trip sometimes exposed it; that could have been a timing/lifecycle side effect, but this has not been reproduced or proven. The split removed the reporter's incidental route to that state, not a documented full-UI feature.

## Proposed behavior

Keep the current integrated Web UI chat presentation as the default. Offer an explicit choice such as **Integrated web chat** vs **Full Gateway Control UI** for users who select the web interface. In full mode, omit the sidebar-hiding CSS injection and validate the embedded Control UI's navigation without requiring navigation through Settings or a timing-dependent workaround. Avoid redundant native + web navigation: for example, collapse/hide the native session pane while full mode is active, while retaining an obvious way to return to integrated/native navigation. The exact layout is a product decision; it should be explicit rather than accidental duplicate sidebars.

The browser Control UI already supplies the full interface outside the Companion; the request is specifically for the full interface **inside** its WebView. No local config or binary changes were made during this investigation.

Related but distinct: #1677 concerns grouping/naming in the native sidebar, which is visible here.

body:
## Summary

The Windows Hub (Companion) session sidebar renders sessions as a **flat list** and does not reflect the session grouping that the Control UI shows for the same gateway.

## Environment

- OpenClaw Windows Hub **2026.9.8-1**, portable x64 (`OpenClawTray-2026.9.8-1-win-x64.zip`)
- Windows 10 22H2 (build 19045)
- WebView2 Runtime 154.0.4258.422
- Gateway: local, `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`, OpenClaw 2026.9.1, single agent (`main`)

## What I observe

1. I assign sessions to sidebar groups through the gateway sessions API (`sessions.patch` with the group field; the patch result reports it as `category`). The Control UI sidebar immediately shows the grouped sections in the order I set, including newly created groups.
2. The Hub sidebar shows the same sessions but as a **flat list** - no group headers and no grouping/ordering. Inspecting the accessibility tree, each row is exposed as `WorkspaceSession:<sessionKey>` with no group/category information attached.
3. Separately, for three sessions the Hub displayed a name that did **not** match the gateway-side `label` / display name (and did not match the Control UI). After I set an explicit `label` via `sessions.patch`, the Hub displayed that label correctly - so the Hub does honour an explicit `label`, but it appears to fall back to a locally derived name when none is set, and that fallback can diverge from the gateway's own display name.

## Expected / request

- Mirror the Control UI's session groups (and their order) in the Hub sidebar; **or**
- If a flat conversation list is deliberate for the Hub, it would help to (a) document that, and (b) avoid showing a locally derived name that conflicts with the gateway's display name.

## Extra notes

- The Hub sidebar does not list automation/cron sessions at all. That may well be intentional for a conversation-oriented view, but it is another difference from the Control UI session list.
- Verified by reading the live UI in both clients against the same gateway, so this is not a caching/sync artifact on the gateway side.
